args.name: Sela Thorn

properties.role: Tide-reader who rows the only boat that goes near the bell water
properties.played_as: Grey braid, salt-stained coat. Talks in a whisper as if the water might hear, never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line. Shrugs and goes back to mending her net.
properties.wants: Never to row at night; will row the party by day for two silver.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

args.why: New NPC the GM voiced at pier four.

args.name: Bram

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Generous with the party: stew on the house.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: New NPC the GM voiced at the tavern.

args.name: The Tarred Gull

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks. Fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

args.why: New place where the party ended the night.

args.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Forty years ago Saltmere Mine flooded the same night the drowned bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

args.why: Sela links the mine's flooding to the bell's first ringing.

args.name: The Kelp Mother

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles; the table has not seen her.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

args.why: Local belief the GM voiced; the GM did not confirm it is real.

args.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: Bram gives Maren a personal stake in the bay.

args.name: Is Maren in the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master Maren Vosk is running the choir. Only the players' guess; the GM did not confirm it.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

args.why: Player theory, tracked as a thread only.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, about an hour from Gullwick. Entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, half-rotted timber frame, a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of church and old candle wax. About thirty paces in the tunnel floods with warm black water; hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: Flooded inside; the bad air hurt Oren.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

args.why: The party entered the mine and the GM described it.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out: just the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight the bell rang twelve times under the water, with a louder humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor like a congregation, then vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

args.why: The party saw the chapel and the congregation at midnight.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

args.why: The GM advanced the clock from 2 to 3 after the midnight ringing.

properties.next_step: Plan: at first light Sela rows them out and they dive to the drowned chapel at low tide; Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

args.why: The bell rang again with a congregation seen; the party made a plan.

properties.what_changed: In Saltmere Mine, Teo found a hymn-book page with "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin and says it is Mira's handwriting, so she was there. Earlier: Mira heard the bell the night she left.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

args.why: A new clue about Mira; the handwriting ID is Teo's claim.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.

args.why: Sela was last seen at the docks (pier four).

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

args.why: Bram keeps the Tarred Gull.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

args.why: The fact is about Saltmere Mine.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

args.why: The fact is about Maren.

sources.quote: She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

args.why: Vessa raised the theory.

sources.quote: Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

args.why: The theory is about Maren.

args.why: The party ended the night at the inn.
